# Containers and Kubernetes

## Dockerfile

- Use a minimal base image with a version or a digest (for example a distroless or a slim image). Not `latest`.
- Use a multi-stage build: build tools stay in the build stage.
- Run as a non-root user. Set a read-only root file system when the application allows it.
- Order the layers from the least to the most often changed, for the build cache. Copy the lock file and install the dependencies before you copy the source.
- Do not copy secrets into the image. Use build secrets (`--mount=type=secret`) when the build needs them. Keep a `.dockerignore` (exclude `.git`, `.env`, local build output).
- Set a `HEALTHCHECK` only when the platform uses it. Kubernetes uses probes instead.
- Validate with `hadolint`.

## Kubernetes manifest

| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Resources | `requests` for CPU and memory. A memory `limit`. A CPU limit only if the platform team requires it. |
| Probes | `readinessProbe` for traffic, `livenessProbe` only for deadlocks (not for slow dependencies), `startupProbe` for slow starts. |
| Security context | `runAsNonRoot: true`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, drop all capabilities, `readOnlyRootFilesystem` when possible. |
| Availability | At least two replicas for a production service, a `PodDisruptionBudget`, and topology spread or anti-affinity. |
| Scaling | A `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` with metrics that follow the load. |
| Shutdown | `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` longer than the longest request. A `preStop` delay if the load balancer is slow to remove the pod. |
| Configuration | ConfigMaps for configuration. Secrets from the secret manager, not in git. |
| Image | A version tag or a digest. |

## Helm and Kustomize

- Keep the defaults of a chart safe. Put the values for each environment in separate files.
- Validate: `helm lint`, `helm template ... | kubeconform` (the human or a check runs the pipe), `kustomize build`.
